presentation.title: Medicare Benefits Scam Call
presentation.summary: A caller offers a new Medicare card, refund, or free medical device. The scam tries to collect Medicare number, SSN, date of birth, or insurance information.
presentation.practiceGoal: Never give Medicare or personal information to an unexpected caller. Verify unexpected benefits calls independently using an official source.

warningSigns.sign: A caller claims that a new Medicare card is required.
The caller offers free medical equipment or a refund.
The caller threatens that benefits could be lost or paused.
The caller asks for a Medicare number, Social Security number, date of birth, or insurance information.
The caller already knows some personal information and uses it to appear legitimate.

finalReview.safestAction: End the unexpected call and verify the request independently using an official source.

realWorldActions.action: Do not provide your Medicare number or Social Security number to an unexpected caller.
Do not confirm personal information simply because the caller already knows some details.
Contact your doctor or trusted provider before accepting unexpected offers for medical equipment.
Do not allow threats about losing benefits to pressure you into acting immediately.
Use the official contact information on your Medicare card or other trusted documentation to verify the caller.

artifact.heading: The caller says your Medicare card needs to be updated
artifact.message: The caller says, "We're updating Medicare cards. I just need to verify your number." The caller asks for the learner's Medicare number and says the information is needed to make sure benefits continue without interruption.
artifact.transcript: A simulated caller says that Medicare cards are being updated and asks the learner to verify their Medicare number. The caller has contacted the learner unexpectedly and has not been independently verified.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller asks for your Medicare number?
scene.description: An unexpected caller asking for Medicare information should not be trusted without independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The caller claims that a new Medicare card is required.
The caller asks for the Medicare number during an unexpected call.
The caller wants the learner to verify sensitive information immediately.

choice.title: Read the Medicare number
choice.subtitle: Give the caller the Medicare number so they can verify the account.

feedback.heading: Sharing the number creates an identity and benefits fraud risk
feedback.consequence: The caller now has sensitive Medicare information that could be used for fraud.
feedback.explanation: An unexpected caller should not receive your Medicare number simply because they claim to be updating benefits.

warningSigns.sign: The caller requested sensitive information before independent verification.

choice.title: Ask them to mail the information
choice.subtitle: Ask the caller to send information through the mail instead.

feedback.heading: Delaying the decision is safer, but verification is still needed
feedback.consequence: You avoid immediately providing the Medicare number, but the caller may continue trying to persuade you.
feedback.explanation: Do not rely on information supplied by the unexpected caller as proof of identity. Use independently located contact information to verify the request.

warningSigns.sign: The caller initiated the contact unexpectedly.

choice.title: Hang up and call the number on your Medicare card
choice.subtitle: End the unexpected call and verify the request independently.

feedback.heading: You chose independent verification
feedback.consequence: You avoid giving sensitive information to the unexpected caller.
feedback.explanation: Unexpected benefits calls should be verified independently rather than through a phone number or contact information supplied by the caller.

warningSigns.sign: The caller could not independently establish their identity.

artifact.callStatus: Caller claims to know personal details
artifact.heading: Knowing your information does not prove the caller is legitimate
artifact.message: The caller knows the learner's name and address and says, "We already have your information, so you know we're official." The caller then asks the learner to confirm additional information.
artifact.transcript: The simulated caller knows the learner's name and address and uses those details to appear legitimate. The caller then asks the learner to confirm additional personal information.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller already knows your name and address?
scene.description: Known personal details do not prove that a caller is an official representative.

warningSigns.sign: The caller uses information they already know as proof of identity.
Basic personal information may be public or exposed through a data leak.
The caller continues asking for more sensitive information.

choice.title: Trust them because they know your details
choice.subtitle: Assume the caller is legitimate because they know your name and address.

feedback.heading: Known information does not prove identity
feedback.consequence: The caller gains additional credibility without actually proving who they are.
feedback.explanation: Names and addresses can be obtained from public records, previous contacts, or data exposure. They should not be treated as proof that an unexpected caller is legitimate.

warningSigns.sign: The caller is using information they already possess as proof of identity.

choice.title: Ask why they need more information
choice.subtitle: Question the caller about why additional information is necessary.

feedback.heading: Questioning the request is a good warning sign
feedback.consequence: The caller may pressure you or provide another explanation for requesting sensitive information.
feedback.explanation: Asking questions is useful, but the safest response to an unexpected request is to stop the call and verify independently.

warningSigns.sign: The caller still has not independently established their identity.

choice.title: Refuse to confirm anything
choice.subtitle: Do not confirm personal information to the unexpected caller.

feedback.heading: You protected your personal information
feedback.consequence: You prevent the caller from using additional personal information to strengthen the scam.
feedback.explanation: Knowing a few details about you does not establish that the caller is legitimate. Stop the conversation and verify independently.

warningSigns.sign: The caller attempted to use known information as proof of identity.

artifact.heading: The caller offers free medical equipment
artifact.message: The caller says the learner qualifies for a free back brace, test kit, or other medical equipment. The caller asks for doctor and insurance information to process the offer.
artifact.transcript: The simulated caller offers free medical equipment and asks the learner to provide doctor and insurance information. The caller has not been independently verified.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller offers free medical equipment?
scene.description: Unexpected medical equipment offers can be used to collect insurance information or submit fraudulent claims.

warningSigns.sign: The equipment is offered unexpectedly over the phone.
The caller asks for doctor or insurance information.
The caller describes the equipment as free to encourage quick compliance.

choice.title: Accept and provide doctor and insurance information
choice.subtitle: Give the caller the requested information to receive the free equipment.

feedback.heading: The free offer can create a medical billing fraud risk
feedback.consequence: The caller receives insurance information that could potentially be used for fraudulent billing.
feedback.explanation: An unexpected offer of medical equipment should not be accepted by providing insurance information to an unverified caller.

warningSigns.sign: The caller requested insurance information for an unsolicited offer.

choice.title: Ask your doctor first
choice.subtitle: Discuss the equipment with your doctor or trusted medical provider.

feedback.heading: You chose a trusted medical provider
feedback.consequence: You avoid providing insurance information to the unexpected caller.
feedback.explanation: Using a trusted doctor or provider gives you an independent way to determine whether the equipment is actually needed or available.

warningSigns.sign: The caller made the offer without an established relationship.

choice.title: Ask if there is a copay
choice.subtitle: Ask whether you would have to pay anything for the equipment.

feedback.heading: The payment question does not verify the caller
feedback.consequence: The caller may simply say there is no copay and continue requesting information.
feedback.explanation: Whether an offer is free or has a copay does not establish that the caller is legitimate. Verify the offer through a trusted provider.

warningSigns.sign: The caller still has not been independently verified.

artifact.heading: The caller says your benefits could be paused
artifact.message: The caller says, "Your benefits could be paused if you don't act today." The caller pressures the learner to provide information immediately.
artifact.transcript: The simulated caller threatens that the learner's benefits could be paused if action is not taken immediately. The caller uses urgency to pressure the learner into complying.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller says your benefits could be paused today?
scene.description: Threats about losing benefits are designed to create panic and discourage independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The caller creates a deadline.
The caller threatens that benefits could be paused.
The caller wants immediate action before you can verify the claim.

choice.title: Panic and comply
choice.subtitle: Give the caller the requested information because you are worried about losing benefits.

feedback.heading: Urgency caused you to bypass verification
feedback.consequence: The caller receives sensitive information because the threat created pressure to act immediately.
feedback.explanation: Scammers use urgency and threats to make people act before they have time to verify a request.

warningSigns.sign: The caller demanded immediate action.
The caller used a threat about losing benefits.

choice.title: End the call and verify independently
choice.subtitle: Do not comply with the deadline. End the call and verify through a trusted source.

feedback.heading: You stopped the pressure and verified independently
feedback.consequence: You avoid giving sensitive information to the caller and take control of the verification process.
feedback.explanation: Pressure about losing benefits is a warning sign. Ending the call allows you to verify the claim without the scammer controlling the conversation.

warningSigns.sign: The caller attempted to use urgency to prevent independent verification.

choice.title: Ask for a supervisor
choice.subtitle: Request to speak with someone higher up at the organization.

feedback.heading: A supervisor may not provide independent verification
feedback.consequence: The caller may simply transfer you to another person who repeats the same story.
feedback.explanation: Moving to another person within the same unexpected call does not independently verify the organization. End the call and use a trusted contact method instead.

warningSigns.sign: The entire conversation is still controlled by the unexpected caller.

artifact.heading: Protect Medicare information like financial information
artifact.message: Medicare numbers, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, and insurance information are sensitive personal information. Do not provide them to an unexpected caller.
artifact.transcript: The guide reminds the learner to protect Medicare information like financial information. Unexpected calls, free medical equipment offers, requests for sensitive information, and threats about losing benefits are warning signs. When in doubt, end the call and verify independently through a trusted source.

scene.question: What is the safest response to an unexpected Medicare-related call?
scene.description: Protect sensitive information and verify unexpected requests independently.

warningSigns.sign: New-card claims
Free medical equipment offers
Requests for Medicare or Social Security information
Threats about losing benefits
Pressure to act immediately

choice.title: Verify independently and protect your information
choice.subtitle: End unexpected calls and use trusted contact information to verify the request.

feedback.heading: Excellent
feedback.consequence: You recognized the warning signs and avoided giving sensitive information to the caller.
feedback.explanation: Independent verification prevents the unexpected caller from controlling the information used to establish trust.

warningSigns.sign: Unexpected requests for sensitive information should be independently verified.

artifact.heading: Safe verification completed
artifact.message: The unexpected Medicare call was declined or verified independently using an official source.
artifact.transcript: The learner successfully avoided sharing sensitive information, hung up on the caller, or verified the request through trusted official channels.

outcome.label: Medicare benefits verified safely
outcome.heading: You protected your personal and insurance information
outcome.explanation: You avoided falling for unverified benefit updates, fake medical equipment offers, and high-pressure threats by hanging up and verifying independently.

warningSigns.sign: Unexpected benefits or new-card claims.
Urgent threats about pausing benefits.
